slot.brief: For a lanthanide ion (e.g. Eu3+/Gd3+), write the 4f configuration and calculate the magnetic moment using √n(n+2) BM or discuss orbital contribution.

stem: In the spin-only approximation, use $\mu=\sqrt{n(n+2)}$ BM. Which ordered pair of $4f$ configurations and magnetic moments is correct for $\text{Tb}^{3+}$ ($Z=65$) and $\text{Dy}^{3+}$ ($Z=66$)?

verdicts.working: Tb³⁺ is [Xe]4f⁸ (6 unpaired electrons), giving μ = √48 ≈ 6.93 BM. Dy³⁺ is [Xe]4f⁹ (5 unpaired electrons), giving μ = √35 ≈ 5.92 BM.

working:
$\text{Tb}^{3+}: 65-3=62\Rightarrow [\text{Xe}]4f^8,\ n=6;\ \mu=\sqrt{6(8)}=6.93\ \text{BM}$
$\text{Dy}^{3+}: 66-3=63\Rightarrow [\text{Xe}]4f^9,\ n=5;\ \mu=\sqrt{5(7)}=5.92\ \text{BM}$

Independent check: Tb³⁺ is [Xe]4f⁸ (6 unpaired electrons), giving μ = √48 ≈ 6.93 BM. Dy³⁺ is [Xe]4f⁹ (5 unpaired electrons), giving μ = √35 ≈ 5.92 BM.
solution:
Removing three electrons gives Tb³⁺: [Xe]4f⁸ with $n=6$ unpaired electrons, and Dy³⁺: [Xe]4f⁹ with $n=5$ unpaired electrons.
$$\mu_{\text{Tb}^{3+}}=\sqrt{6(6+2)}=6.93\ \text{BM},\qquad \mu_{\text{Dy}^{3+}}=\sqrt{5(5+2)}=5.92\ \text{BM}$$

B: Miscounts the unpaired electrons in the more-than-half-filled $4f$ subshells.
C: Assigns each ion one fewer $4f$ electron than its trivalent configuration.
D: Uses the neutral-atom $4f$ configurations without accounting for ion formation.
